result.title: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics
result.summary: In text-to-SQL and AI-agent analytics, successful SQL execution does not establish semantic correctness under changing business definitions. We study revalidation of fixed queries after changes to refund attribution, tax treatment, eligible populations and exchange-rate dates. An executable verification profile binds the requested revision and knowledge cutoff to legal counterexample data and exact monetary comparison. A preregistered confirmation on 32 newly authored revision families and two local producer bundles retains 192 query-definition cells: 144 nonconforming, 36 finite-suite agreeing and 12 unresolved. Of the nonconforming cells, 63 agree on the current snapshot. At an eight-ledger budget, obligation-guided checking detects 137 discrepancies versus 127 for generic ordering, a paired difference of 6.9 percentage points (family bootstrap 95% interval [2.1, 13.6]; exact family sign-flip p=0.0156). Every ledger arm rejects zero of the 36 agreeing cells. Current-obligation and equal-weight scoring match the guided result, identifying coverage rather than revision-specific priority as the observed source of benefit. Controlled assays, a natural-query pilot and repeated samples provide separate mechanism and robustness evidence. A legal discrepancy refutes conformance; agreement remains restricted to the recorded suite. The study establishes an auditable business-semantic revalidation profile within its authored schema and local-model scope.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究业务定义（退款归因、税务处理、适用人群、汇率日期）变更后，固定 text-to-SQL 查询的再验证问题；提出可执行的验证剖面对照，在 32 个新编修订族、192 个查询-定义单元格上做预注册确认，并在八次台账预算下比较义务引导检查与通用排序的差异检出率。
AI.relevance_reason: 「执行成功不等于语义正确」的区分以及预算受限下按义务排序的证据检查与覆盖优先结论，可能可供核查 LVR 中答案正确但 latent 未承载证据的评价方式与证据获取/停止预算设计；但该工作无视觉输入与 latent 状态，联系属较远领域的类比线索。
